correctness.rationale: For a k-point set of an N-cycle, nonpositive average drift yields a non-halo phase; every maximal halo arc has strictly positive excess density and hence the strict integer bound ceil(k/alpha)-1. For positive drift the whole orbit is the halo and satisfies the same bound. The contiguous k-block gives equality via its k/(j+k) forward prefix averages. The n-dependent max formula then proves the sharp plateau, discontinuity and asymptotic limit, and cycle decomposition handles any finite invariant permutation. Exact-rational checks enumerate every subset for N=2..10 at all finite relevant critical thresholds and their interval midpoints, and test the expected N=10, alpha=3/5 value 8/5; finite checks are not asserted to prove universality.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2015 article gives the general one-sided maximal ergodic weak bound, not the exact finite-orbit cardinality optimum. The October 2026 continuous-time-flow theorem gives 1/alpha for any nontrivial continuous-time flow, which has a different averaging parameter; direct substitution to a finite discrete permutation is invalid. The companion October 2026 theorem treats uncentered balls and Rokhlin-tower transference; its bounded-period plateau is for another basis and does not imply the exact finite one-sided step function. value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the sharp one-sided restricted weak-type constant for every finite cyclic measure-preserving dynamical system, not a single chosen sample. It determines optimal marked-set geometry at each cardinality, all threshold levels, a sharp orbit-length plateau with a discontinuity, extension to arbitrary finite permutations, and monotone recovery of the continuous sharp benchmark. The exact finite-period effect is useful when comparing ergodic maximal estimates for periodic approximants to general flows.
